title: National Monuments under the Antiquities Act
source: Curated selection of significant Antiquities Act designations. Verify against Congressional Research Service report R41330, 'National Monuments and the Antiquities Act,' plus NPS/BLM unit lists and proclamation texts. Acreages are proclaimed figures, approximate.

monuments.name: Petrified Forest
monuments.note: Later enlarged and redesignated a national park (1962).

monuments.name: Devils Tower
monuments.note: The first national monument, proclaimed three months after the Antiquities Act passed.

monuments.name: Grand Canyon
monuments.note: Roosevelt's most aggressive use of the Act — protecting 800,000+ acres as a 'monument.' Upheld by the Supreme Court in 1920 (Cameron v. United States); redesignated a national park in 1919.

monuments.name: Pinnacles
monuments.note: Redesignated a national park in 2013.

monuments.name: Mount Olympus
monuments.note: Core of present-day Olympic National Park (1938).

monuments.name: Dinosaur
monuments.note: Later vastly enlarged; the proposed Echo Park dam here became a landmark 1950s conservation fight.

monuments.name: Bryce Canyon
monuments.note: Redesignated a national park (1928).

monuments.name: Carlsbad Cave
monuments.note: Redesignated Carlsbad Caverns National Park (1930).

monuments.name: Glacier Bay
monuments.note: Redesignated a national park under ANILCA (1980).

monuments.name: Death Valley
monuments.note: Redesignated a national park (1994).

monuments.name: Saguaro
monuments.note: Redesignated a national park (1994).

monuments.name: Joshua Tree
monuments.note: Redesignated a national park (1994).

monuments.name: Capitol Reef
monuments.note: Redesignated a national park (1971).

monuments.name: Jackson Hole
monuments.note: Bitterly contested — Wyoming's delegation responded by amending the Antiquities Act in 1950 to bar any further monuments in Wyoming without Congress. Folded into Grand Teton National Park (1950).

monuments.name: Marble Canyon
monuments.note: Added to Grand Canyon National Park (1975).

monuments.name: Wrangell–St. Elias
monuments.note: Part of Carter's December 1978 Alaska designations; redesignated a national park under ANILCA (1980).

monuments.name: Gates of the Arctic
monuments.note: December 1978 Alaska designation; national park under ANILCA (1980).

monuments.name: Misty Fjords
monuments.note: December 1978 Alaska designation, managed by the Forest Service in the Tongass.

monuments.name: Katmai (expansion)
monuments.note: One of the 1978 Alaska monument actions; national park under ANILCA (1980).

monuments.name: Admiralty Island
monuments.note: December 1978 Alaska designation, Tongass National Forest.

monuments.name: Grand Staircase–Escalante
monuments.note: Announced from the Arizona rim during the 1996 campaign — the first major BLM-managed monument and a lasting Utah grievance. Reduced by Trump (2017), restored by Biden (2021).

monuments.name: Cascade–Siskiyou
monuments.note: Later expanded by Obama (2017).

monuments.name: Bears Ears
monuments.note: Proposed by a coalition of five tribes; the flashpoint of the modern monument fight. Reduced ~85% by Trump (2017), restored by Biden (2021).

monuments.name: Gold Butte
monuments.note: Adjacent to the Bundy ranch near Bunkerville — designated two years after the 2014 armed standoff over unpaid grazing fees on the surrounding BLM land.

monuments.name: Baaj Nwaavjo I'tah Kukveni–Grand Canyon
monuments.note: Protects lands around the Grand Canyon long sought by regional tribes; opposed by Arizona's mining interests.

monuments.name: Avi Kwa Ame
monuments.note: Proposed by the Fort Mojave and other tribes.

modifications.name: Grand Staircase–Escalante
modifications.note: Cut roughly in half — the largest rollback of monument protection in U.S. history, alongside Bears Ears.

modifications.name: Bears Ears
modifications.note: Cut ~85%, from 1.35M to ~202,000 acres. Immediately litigated by tribes and conservation groups.

modifications.name: Cascade–Siskiyou
modifications.note: Expanded by ~48,000 acres in the final days of the Obama administration.

modifications.name: Bears Ears
modifications.note: Restored and slightly enlarged the original boundary.
